verdict.reasoning: Patient states a 'blinding headache for a few days' and that she 'find it very hard to focus or, like I can't even go to work.' Doctor later clarifies it started three days ago.

Patient: 'it just started all of a sudden. I woke up one morning with a headache, and that was three days ago, and I just keep having it.' and 'Kinda all the time.' supports sudden onset on waking and constant course.
Patient: 'it's kind of all over but, I feel like over my right eye, it's um bit, stronger.' supports global headache worse over the right eye.
Patient rates severity: 'mostly, eight, and then it kinda comes down to maybe a five.' and says ibuprofen 'gets a little bit better but like, doesn't go away.'

Photophobia: 'lights definitely make me more sensitive'; visual phenomena: 'I get this, shooting light sometimes'; nausea: 'feeling a bit sick, but no vomiting'; presence on waking: 'I can wake up with it in the morning.'

Patient denies numbness/tingling/weakness ('Um, no.'), smell or taste change ('No, none at all.'), fever ('I don't really feel, feverish'), URI symptoms/cough/flux/hemoptysis ('No, no.' and 'No.'), and weight change ('Um, no change of weight').

Prior headaches: 'a one for like two days, um, but it just went away with Ibuprofen'; earlier: 'a bit of a pressure, in between my eyes... But nothing major.' and denies visual symptoms, nausea, vomiting with past headaches: 'No nothing, none of those.'
Patient: 'yeah, actually had one [eye check] recently and, nothing changed my vision.'

When asked about other medical problems: 'I think I only had a, a pain, um, when I was younger but, no causes found and that went away, but that's, the only thing I know of.' implies no significant ongoing conditions.
Patient: 'apart from the Ibuprofen that I take, sometimes when, the headache gets really bad, nothing else.' supports PRN ibuprofen use.

Patient confirms 'just the pill' and started 'about a year ago.' The doctor later refers to 'that pill' in context of combined pill; in usual practice this is a combined oral contraceptive. This is a reasonable clinical inference.
When asked about allergies: 'Um, and any allergies to anything?' Patient: 'No.' implies no known drug allergies.
Patient: 'my mum like, she has quite bad migraines, she's like, has the vomiting and everything.'
Lives alone: 'Who do you live with at home?' Patient: 'Uh, just by myself.' Works from home: 'Um, I work from home but, couldn't really manage to, do it all the time.'
Patient: 'I work from home but, couldn't really manage... So sometimes I just took a day off.' and detailed missed work over three days due to headache.
Smoking: 'Do you smoke?' 'Uh, no.' Alcohol: 'Do you drink any alcohol regularly?' 'Yeah.' 'probably like, three , once a week.' reasonably supports ~3 units once weekly.
Travel: 'Have you been abroad recently at all?' Patient: 'No.'

Transcript documents acute severe headache for three days with photophobia and visual phenomena, and doctor says 'it, it, it could possibly be a migraine type headache.' This matches the summary of likely migraine.

Doctor links pill and migraine with aura: 'because sometimes if we, if we do think it's a migraine, then you would have to change your pill. If you've had these flashing lights...' indicating combined pill may be contraindicated if migraine with aura.

Doctor: 'we'll check your blood pressure as well... because sometimes if we, if we do think it's a migraine, then you would have to change your pill.' This reflects need to review contraception in context of potential migraine with aura.
Impact on work: initially patient 'can't even go to work' and later describing days off and inability to focus on work due to headache.

Doctor: 'we probably should, book you into an appointment to get an examination... we should do a neurological examination, look at the back of your eyes as well.' and later: 'we'll check your blood pressure as well.'

Doctor: 'I can prescribe you something, similar to Ibuprofen, but a bit stronger... And you can also take Paracetamol at the same time... take it with food.' indicates a stronger NSAID plus paracetamol with food.

Doctor: 'if in the meantime before your appointment your, headache is getting unbearable, getting worse or changing. Then , um, if it's that bad, then you should go to A and E... Um, , you can call us for further advice on that.'
Doctor: 'if it settles, in the meantime then, we can cancel that.' referring to the booked examination appointment.

If you've had these flashing lights...' and 'that pill... wouldn't be suitable to stay on that pill, particularly, we'd have to change it to something else.' supports reviewing/altering combined pill if migraine with aura confirmed.
